OTHER PRESENT:

GP V MANU THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 19.02.2019, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WP(C).No. 4738 of 2019 2  JUDGMENT
The petitioner has approached this Court challenging Ext.P11 order rejecting his application for licence under the Food Safety and Standards Act.
The contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner was not properly put on notice of the defects in his application and that as such, the rejection was completely unjustifiable.

2. The learned Government Pleader appearing for the respondents would contend that the petitioner's application had been returned for rectification on 26.12.2018, since the trade licence issued by the Corporation of Thiruvananthapuram was in the name of Sri. Cyril Fernandez and not in the petitioner's name.
The petitioner was also required to upload the D&O licence for the current year.
It is stated that since no reply had been received from the petitioner within the prescribed time of 30 days, the petitioner's application had been rejected.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner was never put on notice as to the requirements/rectification necessary in his application.

In any view of the matter, since the question is with regard to the grant of an FSSAI licence, in case the petitioner submits a fresh application along with all required documents including copies of D&O licences and trade licences, if any, the application will be considered without delay by the respondents.

In case the petitioner submits the application within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, the said application will be taken up, considered and appropriate orders passed thereon, within a period of three weeks thereafter.
The writ petition is ordered accordingly.

Sd/-
